summary: Joseph Tiefenthaler was a Jesuit missionary active in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology from 1729 to 1773. He served as Rector at Agra Jesuit College from circa 1744 to 1747.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and presided over the Société Asiatique.

Linguist Joseph Vendryes studied under Antoine Meillet, Victor Henry, Sylvain Lévi, and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held teaching posts at the University of Paris (1907–1946), the École Normale Supérieure (1920–1936), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1926–1952).

Joseph Virgil Grohmann was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He later served as a professor at Prager Handelsakademie, director at Leitmeritzer Oberrealschule, and Referent at the Landesschulrat.

Joseph Walker Jasper Ouseley was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He served as professor at Fort William College and the East India Company College, and later as Examiner in Oriental Languages for the Civil Service Commission.
Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini. He was affiliated with Loyola University Chicago in 1998.

Linguist Joseph Wright studied at Yorkshire College, Heidelberg University, and Leipzig, earning his Ph.D. under Hermann Osthoff. He later taught at the University of Oxford and served as Professor of Comparative Philology at Corpus Christi College, Oxford.

Joseph van den Gheyn was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He taught at KU Leuven and Institut Catholique de Paris, and served as manuscript conservator at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall was an Austrian scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences from circa 1847 to 1849.
Josho Nozawa was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi. In 1950, he held a professorship at Koyasan University.
Buddhist studies teacher Joshu Sasaki studied at Zuiryo-ji under Joten Soko Miura. He served as abbot at Yotoku-in and Shojuan, founded the Mount Baldy Zen Center, and served as its abbot until 2012.
Joshua Ereshefsky is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who is attested as a Ph.D. candidate at McMaster University in 2026, studying under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn.
Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and linguistics who studied at Bristol Baptist College and under Johannes Lassar. He founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua Timothy Katz studied linguistics at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. A linguist, he was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute around 2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Wangyal. He was affiliated with the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center in 2004.

Linguist Joshua Whatmough completed degrees at the University of Manchester and Emmanuel College. He served as Lecturer in Classics at Bangor University, Professor of Latin at Cairo University, and became a professor at Harvard University in 1926.

Philosopher Josiah Royce studied at the University of California, Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins. He held an instructorship at UC Berkeley from 1878 to 1882 before joining the Harvard University faculty, serving from 1882 to 1916.

Josip Florschütz was an Indologist and linguist who received his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna in 1885. In 1908, he became an extraordinary professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics, Sanskrit, Lithuanian, Gothic, and Albanian at the University of Zagreb.

José Alemany y Bolufer was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Pedro Roca y López and completed his doctorate at Complutense University of Madrid. He held chairs of Greek at the University of Granada and Complutense University of Madrid.

José Canedo Grille was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Seminario Mayor de Santiago de Compostela, University of Granada, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held a post at Heidelberg University in 1943.
